page: Microsoft Azure F64als_v6 is an x86_64 server instance belonging to the Falsv6 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 64 physical cores and 64 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs.

Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in multi-core processing, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores all ranking in the top 10% of tested servers. The processor's instruction set includes AVX-512 and cryptography extensions, contributing to top-tier results in PassMark extended instructions and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is also in the top 10%, while large block read and write bandwidths fall in the top 25%.

The primary tradeoff of the F64als_v6 is its low memory density of 2.0 GB per vCPU, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive databases or large in-memory datasets. However, the high core count and strong compute performance make it highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. Factual workload fits include software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, static web serving, and multi-threaded data decompression.
